findings.message: The new guard `message.message_class == "bug_report" and getattr(verdict, "kind", None) != "bug"` catches every non-author verdict. TriageTombstone and TriageDecision have no `kind`, so any bug report that triage correctly tombstones as a duplicate or turns into a decision is skipped instead of going to `_apply`. It stays pending forever and is re-triaged, with a fresh LLM call, on every pass. That is a hold with no release path.
findings.paved_road: Apply the kind check only to authoring, e.g. `if isinstance(verdict, TriageAuthor) and message.message_class == "bug_report" and verdict.kind != "bug"`. Let tombstone and decision verdicts reach `_apply`. Add a test showing a tombstoned bug_report gets resolved.

findings.message: When `inbox` is set, `box()` calls `inbox_consumer` on every poll, and that always awaits `triage.run`. The old `pending()` gate is gone on this path. `Triage.run` does a git rev_parse, builds a driver, and always appends a `triage_pass` signal to the journal, even when nothing is pending. With an idle inbox configured, the journal gets one record every POLL_SECONDS forever. The journal is the record, not a debug log.
findings.paved_road: Consume the inbox first, then run triage only if `triage.box.pending()` is non-empty. Either gate inside `inbox_consumer`, or call `inbox.consume()` and then keep the existing `if triage.box.pending(): await box_consumer(...)` branch. The serve test still covers the case where Box starts empty, because the report is ingested before the pending check.

findings.message: Acceptance criteria 1 and 2 are not really proven. `test_invalid_metadata_is_rejected_before_replay_read` creates no replay file, so the report would be rejected (unreadable replay) even if the replay were read before metadata validation; the test cannot tell the two orders apart. In `test_actual_replay_and_excerpt_caps_precede_box_recording`, the excerpt report points at the same oversize `replay.json`, so it would be rejected by the replay cap even if the 64 KiB excerpt cap were removed.
findings.paved_road: For ordering, give a bad-metadata report a valid replay file and assert the replay was never read, e.g. with a spy Filesystem that records `read` calls, or a replay path that raises if touched. For the excerpt cap, point the oversized-excerpt report at its own valid small replay file so the excerpt cap is the only reason for rejection.

findings.message: I'm less sure this one is in scope. `_metadata` reads the whole `*.report.json` into memory with no byte limit before validation. The 64 KiB excerpt cap only applies after parsing, so a huge report file is loaded in full on every poll. Also, successfully consumed reports are never moved or removed, so every poll re-reads and re-parses every past report forever, which only the `by_origin` duplicate check short-circuits. The ticket says not to retain unbounded evidence.
findings.paved_road: Before reading a report file, check its size against a fixed limit (about LOG_EXCERPT_LIMIT plus metadata headroom) and reject anything larger. After a successful enqueue or a duplicate match, move the report out of the scan glob (e.g. rename to `.filed`), the same way rejected reports are renamed to `.rejected`.

Fixture-host evidence needs durable custody before sequential triage can author a bug ticket.

## Scope in
Enforce the version-1 report schema, metadata-first 1 MiB replay-file and 64 KiB log-excerpt caps, copy bounded evidence into durable Box custody before recording the message, wire the daemon consumer, and make sequential triage author `kind: bug` tickets whose evidence and `## Regression` survive intake. ## Scope out
Do not retain unbounded evidence, bypass Box custody, or use the delimiter-carrying triage test as Context.

## Output format
Exactly one JSON object and nothing else -- no prose before or after, no
code fence:

{"verdict": "approve" | "snag" | "rma",
 "summary": "<one or two sentences>",
 "findings": [{"code": "correctness_review",
               "path": "<repo-relative path from the diff, or null>",
               "line": <line number in the NEW file, or null>,
               "message": "<what is wrong, concretely>",
               "paved_road": "<what to do instead>"}]}

`findings` is `[]` exactly when `verdict` is `approve`. `code` is always
`correctness_review`. `path` is the path as written in the diff header
without the `a/` or `b/` prefix.

input would contain>"}]}`. If the inputs are reviewable but you are unsure
whether something is a defect, report it as a finding with your
uncertainty stated in the message: a snag costs one rework round, a missed
defect costs a merged bug.
